title: Engine Electronic Control Unit — Disconnection of the Control Harness Channels

ata.title: Engine Fuel Control — Electronic Control Unit

abstract: Disconnection of both channels of the engine electronic control harness at the control unit, with the route recording and the connector protection required before a harness re-route.

sections.purpose: This task gives the procedure to disconnect both channels of the engine electronic control harness at the control unit, and to record the installed route before any re-routing work begins.
sections.job_setup_note: The control unit holds a residual charge and must be given the discharge period stated in the figure before the connectors are disturbed. The two channel connectors are keyed differently but the harness identification sleeves are the primary means of identification and must be checked before disconnection. The installed route must be photographed and recorded before any clamp is released, because on an unmodified engine it is not the route shown in the wiring manual.
sections.procedure: 1. Confirm that the engine has been shut down for the cooling period and that the fuel system is isolated. 2. Open the fan cowl doors and unlatch the core cowl. 3. Let the control unit discharge for the period stated in the figure. WARNING: DO NOT DISTURB THE CONTROL UNIT CONNECTORS BEFORE THE DISCHARGE PERIOD HAS ELAPSED. THE UNIT HOLDS A RESIDUAL CHARGE. 4. Photograph and record the installed route of both channels, including every clamp position. 5. Check the harness identification sleeve on each channel against the wiring manual before you disconnect. CAUTION: DO NOT RELY ON CONNECTOR KEYING ALONE. THE KEYING PREVENTS A CROSSED CONNECTION AT THE UNIT BUT NOT A CROSSED ROUTE AT THE FAN CASE. 6. Disconnect channel A at the control unit and fit the protective cap. 7. Disconnect channel B and fit the protective cap. 8. Release the channel B clamps in sequence from the unit outwards, keeping the count. 9. Lay channel B clear of the fan case and support it. 10. Examine both connector faces for contamination and record the condition. 11. Examine the released clamps for the fire-rated marking and record which standard was fitted.
sections.close_out: Confirm that both connectors are capped and that no harness is left resting on the fan case or on a fuel line. Record the clamp count released, the clamp standard found and the connector face condition. Retain the route photographs with the work package; they are the reference if the re-route has to be reversed.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. Step 11 is mandatory on aircraft pre MOD-148830 to establish the clamp standard fitted.

safety_precautions: Confirm that the fuel system is isolated.
Let the control unit discharge before the connectors are disturbed.
Confirm the engine cooling period has elapsed.
